title: Find the planted defects in a Rust file
description: The model is asked to review a Rust file that contains three deliberately planted defects. Each expected finding is anchored to a keyword that any correct review must contain, so the grade is deterministic rather than a judgement call about prose.
why_it_matters: Review quality is the eval that decides whether a cheaper model can take PR review off the factory's critical path. It needs a known right answer, and it needs to be able to measure false positives — a reviewer that flags everything scores as well as one that flags nothing.
prompt:
You are reviewing a Rust file for real production defects.

The file `qa_verdicts.rs` is reproduced in full below.

Context: it models QA-verdict parsing for a task-tracking workflow. The wire types are modelled after a Tasks API v1 JSON API; the structs are deserialised from that JSON, and the verdict functions decide whether a QA verdict is stale and whether a QA agent's note reports a deferral.

Find real defects:
- places where the code misbehaves on realistic inputs (including the real API JSON shape, not just the shape the tests construct)
- places where a documented contract in a doc comment is not upheld by the code
- places where a unit test would pass while the production path fails

Ignore style, naming, missing docs, clippy lints, or error-handling preferences unless they cause wrong behaviour. Do not modify any file. Do not post comments anywhere.

Reply in EXACTLY this format, one block per finding, nothing else before or after:

FINDING: <short title>
LOC: <line number or line range>
EXPLAIN: <the exact input or condition that breaks it, and the resulting wrong behaviour>
FIX: <suggested fix>

If you find no defects, reply with exactly: NO FINDINGS
Cap yourself at 6 findings, most defensible first.

expected_findings.summary: TaskComment has no camelCase rename, so createdAt never deserialises into created_at and the stale-verdict guard sees no timestamps.
qa_agent_deferred negates against the original-case note and the literal 'no deferred', so a clean verification reads as a deferral.
The evidence capture group [^)]+ stops at the first ')', truncating a test id that contains a nested parenthetical.

must_not_mention.summary: severity_rank's match arms are correct and must not be reported as a defect.
